sentences.text: Ratchasimasaurus belongs to the group of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaurs.
The single known species, R. suranareae, honors the nineteenth-century war heroine Thao Suranari.
A distinctive feature of this animal is its long and flat lower jaw bone.
In the holotype specimen, this jaw measures exactly 198.1 millimeters in length.
Scientists Shibata, Jintasakul, and Azuma formally named the genus in 2011.
The original specimen resides at the Northeastern Research Institute of Petrified Wood and Mineral Resources, while a mounted skeleton is shown in River City, Bangkok.
The animal possesses anatomical traits common to Styracosterna.
It shows a blend of ancient and modern Iguanodontian features, such as a backward-leaning coronoid process and a specialized cheek shelf.
Taxonomists place Ratchasimasaurus within the family Iguanodontidae.
The broader parent group for this animal is Hadrosauroidea.
This dinosaur lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian stage, in the Khok Kruat Formation of Nakhon Ratchasima province, northeastern Thailand.
Its existence spanned the middle of the Cretaceous period, roughly between 120 and 113 million years ago, covering the Aptian to Albian stages.
